title: AI Solution Lifecycle
description: Explains how an individual AI use case, model, agent, application, or product moves from intake through retirement across 14 solution steps.

steps.title: Intake and Registration
steps.purpose: Log, catalogue, and assign ownership for new AI use case proposals.

steps.title: Risk Classification
steps.purpose: Evaluate risk tier, impact level, regulatory exposure, and human oversight requirements.

steps.title: Feasibility and Business Case
steps.purpose: Validate economic ROI, technical feasibility, operational readiness, and funding.

steps.title: Data Readiness
steps.purpose: Verify data quality, lineage, consent, licensing, privacy, and pipeline infrastructure.

steps.title: Solution Design
steps.purpose: Specify functional, technical, security, RAG, agentic, and integration architecture.

steps.title: Model or Agent Selection
steps.purpose: Select foundation models, prompt strategies, agent frameworks, or commercial tools.

steps.title: Build and Configuration
steps.purpose: Develop code, configure prompts/RAG, integrate APIs, and establish security controls.

steps.title: Testing and Evaluation
steps.purpose: Execute red-teaming, safety evaluations, bias checks, performance tests, and user acceptance.

steps.title: Approval and Release
steps.purpose: Formal review by governance board for deployment authorization.

steps.title: Deployment
steps.purpose: Promote solution to production runtime environment with cutover guardrails.

steps.title: Monitoring and Assurance
steps.purpose: Track model drift, latency, cost, prompt misuse, guardrail triggers, and user feedback.

steps.title: Change Management
steps.purpose: Govern model updates, prompt tuning, dataset updates, and scope expansions.

steps.title: Incident Management
steps.purpose: Detect, respond to, mitigate, and record AI safety, security, or output failures.

steps.title: Retirement
steps.purpose: Decommission AI use cases, archive data/prompts, update asset register, and transfer users.
